newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Drillsearch wins Albania oil field approval.
newsitem.headline: Drillsearch wins Albania oil field approval.

text.p: Drillsearch Energy NL said on Wednesday it had won approval from the Albanian government to participate in redevelopment of the Cakran-Mollag and Ballsh-Hekal oil fields in southern Albania.

Drillsearch managing director Philip Kelso told Reuters that Drillsearch would work with the Albanian state oil company, Albpetrol, and two Australian partners to introduce western technology to the projects.
The Cakran-Mollaj field currently produces 900 barrels of 37 American Petroleum Institute (API) grade oil per day, he said.

Cakran-Mollaj has estimated proven oil reserves of around 300 million barrels, with 60 million remaining to be recovered by primary methods, Kelso said. Recovery could be enhanced at a later date using more modern technologies, he said.
Proved recoverable gas reserves are estimated at 106 billion cubic feet, he said.
"There is a lot of potential in Albania," Kelso said.
The Ballsh-Hekal field has estimated proven oil reserves of between 290 and 400 million barrels of 17 API oil, he said.
Roughly 12 percent, or 34 million barrels of oil, remain to be recovered using basic drilling techniques, he said.
Proven recoverable gas reserves are estimated at 36 billion cubic feet. The field is currently producing approximately 200 barrels of oil per day (BPD).
Drillsearch's share of enhanced oil production from the fields should reach about 1,500 bpd in the second year and increase significantly in following years, Kelso said.
Drillsearch and Kiwi International Resources Ltd each hold a 47.5 percent stake in the project. Kitari Oil Pty Ltd, holds the remaining five precent and is operator.
Over the first 18 months of the project, the partners will spend about US$6 million.
Foreign interest in Albania is increasing despite recent political turmoil in the former communist bloc country, Kelso said.

U.K.-based Premier Oil Plc operates the Patos-Marinze field immediately to the north of the Cakran-Mollaj field and other foreign companies, including Royal/Dutch Shell Fountain Oil Inc and OMV are becoming active in the country, he said.
